text:
The Detroit Lions (5-2) are back on the road in Week 9, traveling to Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins (1-6). The Lions held a walkthrough on Wednesday instead of a full practice, so all participation levels are estimates from the coaching staff based on how the player would have participated in a traditional practice.

With that in mind, let’s look at Wednesday’s injury report and get you up to date on what we know.

Note: Any changes from the most recent injury report will be bolded.

RB Isiah Pacheco (MCL/Back, IR) — expected to be out until December

OL Giovanni Manu (undisclosed, NFI) — eligible to begin practicing at any time

OL Ben Bartch (foot, IR) — eligible to begin practicing in Week 10

LB Devin White (forearm, IR) — eligible to begin practicing in Week 10

LB Jimmy Rolder (hamstring, IR) — Season-ending injury

S Kerby Joseph (knee, PUP) — Injury evaluation clock started

S Thomas Harper (ankle, IR) — Eligible to begin practicing at any time

Rolder injured his hamstring last Sunday, and with the injury potentially requiring surgery, he’s being shut down for the remainder of the season. While that ends his rookie season, the good news is he should be able to return in 2027.

I wanted to take a moment to talk about Jack Campbell, as most Lions fans are anxiously awaiting updates on his status and wondering about his future, both on and off the field. First, in case you missed it, Jack Campbell released a statement earlier on Wednesday; here’s an excerpt (emphasis is the author’s):

“I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better.”

Jack is still on the 53-man roster and hasn’t been moved to injured reserve, but it would be improper to speculate why a move has or hasn’t been made at this time. The team typically takes their time in these situations, so it’s important to be patient right now and not make assumptions either way.

Estimated no practice

C Cade Mays (ankle) — Injured in Week 8 — Preparing for Juice Scruggs to start

EDGE DJ Wonnum (concussion) — Injured in Week 8

LB Jack Campbell (neck) — Injured in Week 8

CB D.J. Reed (hip) — Injured in Week 8

Mays reportedly has a “low” ankle injury, which typically sidelines players from one to six weeks (high ankle injuries usually last four to 12 weeks), and while we don’t know how long this will sideline the Lions’ starting center, Dan Campbell did note that he missing Wednesday’s practice was planned and Thursday’s practice could also be in jeopardy. For now, the team is preparing to turn to Juice Scruggs against the Dolphins.

Wonnum is in the NFL’s concussion protocol and must pass a series of steps before he can move forward. Every player deals with head injuries differently, so we will have to wait and see how he is able to handle the increasing stressors deployed in the protocol.

Reed was forced out of the Vikings game late, and while he didn’t return, he was available in the locker room after the game, which is typically a good sign for his injury. The Lions will likely take it slow with their top corner this week.

Estimated limited practice

RB Jacob Saylors (neck) — Injured in Week 8

Saylors was limited early in practices in Week 8 with a neck injury, and while he did not carry an injury designation into the game against the Vikings, he did exit with a reported neck injury. It’s unclear whether this is a new injury or a tweak of the existing one, but it’s not surprising to see him get early-week rest to allow more time to recover.

Last week, St. Brown was dealing with an ankle injury, and now he’s dealing with a rib injury. He left Sunday’s game against the Vikings briefly but did not miss much time before returning.

Ogbongbemiga is dealing with a toe injury, which could leave Detroit’s linebacker room a little short this week, but given he’s just listed as limited, there is plenty of time for him to recover. He could play a bigger special teams role this week, with Malcolm Rodriguez and Trevor Nowaske expected to play bigger defensive roles.

On Tuesday, coach Dan Campbell discussed the timeline for Kerby Joseph, noting that he won’t play in Miami this weekend, as he’s still slowly acclimating back to football activities.

“We’re going to try and give him some scout team reps. He’s not going to play this game,” Campbell said. “I know that (question) was coming. He’s not playing vs. Miami. He’s just going to get some reps in practice.”

Branch, like Wonnum, must go through the NFL’s structured concussion protocol, but an estimated limited practice is a positive sign he could play this week.

title: Coach: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold ruled out with quad injury, is week-to-week - ESPN

RENTON, Wash. -- Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will miss the team's game against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday due to a quad injury, coach Mike Macdonald announced Wednesday.
"We'll be getting both guys ready to play," Macdonald said.
Macdonald said Darnold could likely play through the cracked rib if not for the quad injury.

text:
RENTON, Wash. -- Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will miss the team's game against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday due to a quad injury, coach Mike Macdonald announced Wednesday.

Darnold is week-to-week and will not be placed on injured reserve, per Macdonald. He said Darnold has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders.

The Seahawks' plan is for backup Drew Lock to start against Arizona, but he's still dealing with an injury to his throwing elbow that caused him to be inactive the past two games. Macdonald acknowledged the possibility that Seattle may have to turn to QB3 Jalen Milroe depending on how Lock progresses.

"We'll be getting both guys ready to play," Macdonald said. "We've got full confidence in those guys, and we have a plan in place and we'll go execute it."

Seattle may be adding another quarterback this week, per Macdonald.

Darnold injured his quad on the final drive of the Seahawks' 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears on Monday night, which dropped the reigning Super Bowl champions to 4-4. Macdonald said he also suffered a cracked rib on the second play of the game, when he was hit hard while throwing by blitzing cornerback Kyler Gordon.

Macdonald wasn't aware of the rib injury until after the game, he said. Darnold went 17-of-34 passing for 188 yards, two touchdowns and one interception against Chicago. He was sacked three times and took six official QB hits. His off-target percentage of 29.4% was his highest in the six games he has played since he returned in Week 3 from a glute injury.

"This guy, he's tough as nails," Macdonald said. "I just asked if I could share this, but he cracked his rib on the second play of the game. So he's playing the whole game without even making a thing of it and playing his tail off and competing. I think it's worth noting how tough this guy is. He'll be back sooner than later, I'm sure."

Macdonald said Darnold could likely play through the cracked rib if not for the quad injury. They're the latest setbacks in what's been a tumultuous season for the quarterback. He suffered a glute injury on the fifth play of the season opener, which caused him to miss the remainder of that game and the following week.

"I know it's a challenge, but I've got a lot of respect for how he goes through these things because he goes through it," Macdonald said. "There's no blink, there's no flinch. It's a very matter-of-fact, attacking mentality, which I think that's reflective of the rest of our team, which I appreciate."

Since returning in Week 3, Darnold has thrown nine interceptions in six games. He's completed just over 60% of his passes in that span, with 10 touchdown passes and a Total QBR of 50.8 that ranks 22nd.

Lock, meanwhile, did not commit a turnover while playing most of the first two games. The eighth-year veteran completed nearly 73% of his passes and posted a Total QBR of 82.5 that ranked sixth in that span. Three of his four touchdown passes came in a 31-7 win over Arizona in Week 2, which moved Seattle to 2-0.

Lock was listed as limited on all nine injury reports the Seahawks released from Weeks 6-8, starting on Oct. 11. He was questionable for the last two games before being ruled inactive, though he dressed both times as the emergency third quarterback. He was not seen throwing alongside Darnold and Milroe during warmups before either game.

"He's able to throw," Macdonald said of Lock. "How much, we're working through that right now. But that's the best way to put it ... He's going to throw the ball throughout the week, but we're just going to manage it. He's not going to take 8,000 throws."

Lock suffered the injury during a rainy practice, per Macdonald. He did not specify the date.

"It's an elbow injury," Macdonald said. "All the fancy names, I can't explain that to you, but he hasn't throw much."

The Seahawks drafted Milroe in the third round in 2025 with a plan to take advantage of his running ability in specialty packages while he developed as a passer. But after early fumbling issues, he hasn't seen the field during a regular-season game since Week 5 of last year.

Macdonald said Lock and Milroe will be "splitting reps for a certain amount of time" this week. They're holding a walk-through Wednesday.

"I think we've just got to take it day by day at this time," he said. "But Jalen will take some practice reps as well. Today's a slow day, so it's kind of hard to tell. We have a plan for Drew to get some live throws later, but I think it's just one of those things where we kind of have to work it day-in and day-out and figure out what's the best way to get him to Sunday."

text:
One of the the top playmakers who could be available at the 2026 NFL trade deadline is now in the concussion protocol.

New York Jets coach Aaron Glenn told reporters on Wednesday that 2022 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year wide receiver Garrett Wilson is in the concussion protocol. Wilson leads the Jets in targets (63), catches (43), receiving yards (527) and receiving touchdowns (3) this season, and his four-year, $130 million contract extension is set to kick in next season.

It sounds inconceivable that the rebuilding Jets would part with a 26-year-old who has been one of the team's faces, but Wilson showed public signs of frustration in their loss to the previously winless Miami Dolphins in Week 7. CBS cameras caught Wilson appearing to yell at quarterback Geno Smith and passing game coordinator Seth Ryan. After the game, Wilson said it was a constructive conversation.

"We were collaborating," said Wilson, via ESPN. "I don't even think I was talking to Geno. I think we were both heated, but not at each other at all. We were just disappointed with how we were playing up to that point and wanted to be a little more aggressive. That's what that was."

Wilson wants to "make an impact" and it will be interesting to see if that will remain to be with the Jets, who are 2-6, long term with the Nov. 10 trade deadline looming.

"Just trying to figure out how we can fix where we're at right now, wanting to get it in our hands and make a difference and try to win these games that we feel like we're a better team -- and we're not," Wilson said. "Like I've said before, I want it in my hands to try and make an impact. So that's all we were talking about, just putting it in our hands and how we can make that happen, being aggressive throughout and keeping ourselves out of those situations so we can win these games."

authors: Jordan Raanan, Brady Henderson, Jeff Legwold, Rich Cimini, Mike Kaye, Mike Reiss, NFL Nation, Ben Solak, DJ Bien-Aime, Jeremy Fowler

text:
Detroit Lions All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell released a statement Wednesday saying he has full movement in his lower body and is making progress with movement in his upper body as he recovers from a neck injury, suffered in Sunday's game.

Campbell, who remains hospitalized, was placed on a backboard and carted off the field early in the fourth quarter of a 19-15 win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. He was alert and breathing when he was taken to the hospital.

"I'm incredibly encouraged by the progress I've made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I'm continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body," Campbell said in a statement. "I know there's still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I'm taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better."

Lions coach Dan Campbell said it was powerful that Jack Campbell updated his improving condition himself, shortly before the team's previously scheduled news conferences with coaches and players.

"That's good news. That's positive news," Dan Campbell said. "We're all thankful for that."

Campbell was face down on the turf and not moving Sunday after hitting tight end T.J. Hockenson for his third tackle of the game. Campbell was evaluated by medical personnel before being strapped to a board and carefully lifted onto the cart to a round of applause. Detroit's entire team and most of the coaching staff surrounded the cart.

"I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field," Jack Campbell said in his statement. "I know those were difficult moments, and I'm incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I'll never forget."

The former Iowa star was drafted by the Lions with the 18th overall pick in 2023.

Last season, Campbell was an All-Pro selection after becoming the first NFL player in seven years to have 150-plus tackles and at least five sacks and three forced fumbles.

The Lions signed Campbell last May to a four-year contract extension that runs through the 2030 season.

The Lions (5-2) play at Miami (1-6) on Sunday.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

Baltimore added Austin Reed, who was with the team in the preseason, to its practice squad and signed Kedon Slovis off Green Bay's practice squad earlier this week in an attempt to build some sort of depth on a short week. Reed has never taken a regular-season snap, and Slovis has taken five.

Huntley, 29, has spent six of his seven years with the Ravens after going undrafted in 2020. He has been a crucial depth piece, starting 14 games during his time in Baltimore, including three this year as Jackson dealt with an ankle injury. Huntley guided Baltimore to a win over the Falcons but lost to the Browns and Bengals before Jackson's short-lived return. He suffered the turf toe injury when Bills DT Ed Oliver landed on the back of his foot.

With more clarity on at least one quarterback's injury, the Ravens could look to make a trade ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline, with Tyson Bagent and Jacoby Brissett as potential options mentioned by NFL Network's Ian Rapoport earlier this week.

Baltimore is 4-4 on the season and has lost three straight games.

To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you. This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I'm proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn't ask to be surrounded by a better group of people.

One thing I've learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit. That's exactly how I'm going to approach this challenge.

Please continue to keep me and my family in your prayers. We feel the love, and I can't thank everyone enough.

God is good. My faith is strong.

Jack Campbell

"Anytime, especially being able to hear it from him, that means a lot. That's powerful in itself, more than hearing it from me or anybody else," Lions head coach Dan Campbell told reporters on Wednesday. "Those are his and his family's words, so that's powerful. I know that always helps to know that he's improving. Because at this point, that's all you're looking for, is just to know that he's improving. The status is changing every eight hours, 10 hours, in a good way. It always is going to help."

Campbell is in his fourth season with the Lions. The Iowa product was selected with the No. 18 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft and signed a four-year, $81 million extension that made him one of the highest-paid off-ball linebackers in the NFL this past offseason.

In 2025, Campbell was named a First Team All-Pro and Pro Bowler after recording 176 tackles, nine tackles for loss, five sacks, three forced fumbles and four passes defended.

title: Jets' Garrett Wilson in concussion protocol, Breece Hall trending toward return - ESPN
authors: Rich Cimini, Brady Henderson, Jeff Legwold, Mike Kaye, Mike Reiss, NFL Nation, Ben Solak, DJ Bien-Aime, Jeremy Fowler, Liz Loza

text:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- The New York Jets, losers of three straight, might not have star wide receiver Garrett Wilson for Sunday's road game against the heavily favored Kansas City Chiefs.

Wilson is in concussion protocol and considered day-to-day, coach Aaron Glenn said Wednesday.

While Wilson's status is up in the air, the Jets do expect to have running back Breece Hall (quadriceps) back in the lineup. Hall, sidelined for five games, is "trending in the right direction," Glenn said.

Wilson took a blow to the head while making a reception on the Jets' next-to-last play in their 38-33 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Safety Jeremy Chinn was flagged for unnecessary roughness.

Wilson stayed in the game for the final play, an unsuccessful Hail Mary intended for him in the end zone. On Monday, he reported to the facility experiencing concussion symptoms, according to Glenn.

Hall has been practicing for two weeks, albeit on a limited basis, and was listed as questionable for the last two games. The Jets have been deliberate with Hall, Glenn said, because they don't want to risk further injury.

Braelon Allen's emergence has lessened the need to rush him back. In five games as the starter, Allen has rushed for 504 yards and 5.0 yards per carry. The only player in the NFL with more rushing yards over that stretch is the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' Bucky Irving (548).

Glenn provided a curt answer when asked how he'd manage a Hall-Allen backfield.

"Both will play," he said, declining to elaborate.

Hall, who signed a three-year, $43.5 million contract in the offseason, has been the subject of trade speculation. On Monday, Glenn insisted, "We're in the business of keeping good players, and he's one of our better players. So Breece will still be here."

Wilson leads the Jets in receptions (43), receiving yards (527) and receiving touchdowns (three). The Jets (2-6) have two capable receivers in Adonai Mitchell and rookie Omar Cooper Jr. Mitchell recorded a career-high 147 yards last week; Cooper already has two 100-yard receiving days.

Unfortunately, those occurrences are not out of the norm, and former wide receiver Brandon Marshall has been on the field for a couple of those scary moments, including one that ended a career.

Marshall was a member of the Denver Broncos when his then-teammate, Dominic Hixon, was tackled by Kevin Everett on Sept. 9, 2007. Everett suffered a cervical spine injury that left doctors unsure whether he would ever walk again, but he defied the odds.

During an interview with OutKick, Marshall also recalled a time while playing at UCF when a teammate of his was airlifted to the hospital. Defensive lineman Paul Carrington, who played 15 NFL games, was injured during a practice before the 2005 season started - he wound up playing the entire season and leading the Conference USA with nine sacks.

"Honestly, it comes with it. In those moments, you’re shocked and you’re really feeling for your teammate or the guy on the field. But once the whistle blows, you don’t get wrapped up in your emotions. You have to have a short-term memory. You’re trained to move forward," Marshall said.

The Lions on Monday announced "preliminary indications are positive" for Campbell's condition. But "out of respect for Jack and his family, we will not share further information at this time."

"It's positive, you know?" coach Dan Campbell told reporters. "So your prayers are working. Please continue to do that."

Minnesota Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson caught a pass in the middle of the field and was soon sandwiched by two Lions defenders, including Campbell. Campbell arrived at the contact while falling to his knees and appeared to have his head slanted upward, so he made contact with his facemask rather than his shoulders and arms.

Campbell immediately collapsed and lay motionless, his arms dropping to his sides. On a positive note, Campbell did not require help breathing.

"That's difficult, you know, it's difficult," Dan Campbell said. "You don't ever want to see somebody like that on the field, but when you see Jack, Jack never lays on the field ever, no matter what it is.

title: Jack Campbell updates: What we know as Detroit Lions return to practice

text:
Injured linebacker Jack Campbell said in a statement released by the Detroit Lions on Wednesday, Nov. 4, that he has "full movement" in his lower body, is "continuing to make progress with movement" in his upper body and remains "very optimistic" about his recovery.

"My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers and support we've received over the past few days," the statement read. "It means more to us than words can express."

Campbell was injured making a tackle on tight end T.J. Hockenson on the first play of the fourth quarter of the Lions' win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 1.

Campbell's head appeared to hit Hockenson's left hip on the play. He fell face-first to the ground after making the stop and lay motionless on the turf as doctors loaded him onto a backboard and took him to a waiting ambulance by medical cart.

The game was delayed for about 10 minutes, and Ford Field sat silent while players from both teams surrounded the scene on a knee in prayer.

Campbell remains in the hospital, and he said in his statement he's "incredibly encouraged by the progress I've made in such a short period of time."

"I have full movement in my lower body, and I'm continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body," the statement said. "I know there's still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I'm taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better."

The Lions rallied to beat the Vikings after Campbell's injury, getting a stop on a key fourth-and-5 play on the next snap. Minnesota scored on its next possession to take a 15-12 lead, before the Lions scored the game-winning touchdown.

After the game, Dan Campbell led an emotional locker room in prayer, and players said the win was dedicated to Jack Campbell.

“Just seeing something like that, him being down for so long, yeah, I think from that moment on we really – it was for 4-6, man,” defensive end Aidan Hutchinson said. “And again, we don’t really know the status, but we’re praying for him.”

In his statement, Jack Campbell thanked Lions trainers for their quick response, the doctors in charge of his recovery at Hen Ford Hospital and fans for keeping him in their minds.

"My faith in God has never been stronger," the statement said. "I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we'll get through this."

The entire statement can be read below:

My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we’ve received over the past few days. It means more to us than words can express.

I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better.

My faith in God has never been stronger. I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we’ll get through this.

I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field. I know those were difficult moments, and I’m incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I’ll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you.

I also can’t say enough about the incredible care I’ve received from the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital and the Detroit Lions medical staff. They’ve been amazing to me and my family throughout this process, and I’m truly grateful for everything they’ve done.

To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you. This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I’m proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn’t ask to be surrounded by a better group of people.

One thing I’ve learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit. That’s exactly how I’m going to approach this challenge.

Please continue to keep me and my family in your prayers. We feel the love, and I can’t thank everyone enough.

God is good. My faith is strong.

Jack Campbell

Lions coach Dan Campbell will speak to the media again on Wednesday afternoon and could provide a further update on Campbell's progress.

Here's more of what we know so far:

Scottie Montgomery: 'We're preparing like [Campbell] prepares'

Detroit Lions wide receivers coach Scottie Montgomery spoke at the Lions training facility in Allen Park on Wednesday, saying the "human element" came into play when facing Campbell's injury on Sunday.

"It's very difficult, of course, emotionally, to be in a game like that and have a situation like that happen. But we do have to talk about it. We can't ignore it, we have that open dialogue," he said. "And at the same time, we're honoring him by the way that we prepare. We're preparing like he prepares. That's what we're talking to each other about as players, as coaches, we're going to prepare like he prepared. Play like he plays.

"There's no way around anybody in that locker room not feeling a certain way about it. But that same feeling that causes pain, it causes us to pursue the excellence of what Jack would want us to do in this situation."

Dan Campbell: 'The status is changing every eight hours, 10 hours, in a good way'

Lions coach Dan Campbell spoke briefly on the linebacker's injury in his Wednesday news conference, saying that it was "powerful" to hear Campbell's update from his family.

"That always helps, to know that he's improving," he said. "The status is changing every eight hours, 10 hours, in a good way."

Campbell also revealed that the Lions have mental health resources that some players are using during this time.

Amon-Ra St. Brown shares thoughts

Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown shared his thoughts on Jack Campbell on his podcast, talking about how hard it was to flip the switch back to playing football after seeing his teammate down on the field.

Dan Campbell to speak today

Lions coach Dan Campbell will speak to the media at 1 p.m. ET today. You can watch his news conference below.

Aidan Hutchinson on Jack Campbell injury: 'Just the weirdest feeling'

A few Lions players have shared their feelings on Campbell's injury, with quarterback Jared Goff and edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson both speaking in radio interviews on Tuesday, Nov. 3.

Hutchinson revealed that he has had "the weirdest feeling" in the days after the Campbell injury, while Lions coach Dan Campbell expressed that his players should be thinking about the injured linebacker while also focusing on their jobs.

What happened to Jack Campbell?

Campbell was injured making a tackle on Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson on the first play of the fourth quarter. Campbell's head appeared to hit Hockenson's left hip on the play.

He fell face first to the ground after making the stop and laid motionless on the turf as doctors loaded him on a backboard and took him to a waiting ambulance by medical cart.

The game was delayed for about 10 minutes, and Ford Field sat silent while players from both teams surrounded the scene on a knee in prayer. Several Lions players, including Aidan Hutchinson, Jared Goff, Derrick Barnes, Levi Onwuzurike and Chuck Clark, approached the cart and appeared to say something to Campbell before it left the field, and Barnes said he was headed to the hospital, where Campbell remained overnight, after the game.

"He's got a wife; I know they’re worried because I was worried," Barnes said. "I can only imagine how they feel in those types of moments. Forget football, it’s about the person. Football was the last thing on my mind when that happened. It was all about Jack."

The Lions forced a incomplete pass on fourth-and-5 one play after Campbell's injury, and defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard gathered his unit on the sideline between series.

After the Vikings took a 15-12 lead midway through the fourth quarter, the Lions rallied for the winning touchdown. After the game, players said Campbell was on their mind during the comeback.

“I’ve never really been through something like that, like right when they wheel him off, you go back into it," Hutchinson said. "It was just weird. You got to get back in football mode immediately, but I think we really did a good job of directing the energy and directing that game. ... We were just trying to get the job done with the guys we had for the guys we lost."

How did Jack Campbell get hurt? Video of injury

Here's the video of the injury. It seemed to show Campbell getting bent back on the tackle.

Who is Jack Campbell on the Lions?

Campbell was the No. 18 overall pick by the Lions in 2023 out of Iowa.

Campbell, a 2025 first-team All-Pro selection, is considered one of the best off-ball linebackers in the NFL, and he's one of the highest-paid now.

Jack Campbell contract

The Lions signed Campbell, 26, in May to a four-year contract worth $81 million with $51.4 million guaranteed, keeping him in Detroit through the 2030 season.

text:
After Lions linebacker Jack Campbell was taken off the field on a backboard early in the fourth quarter against the Vikings and transported to a local hospital on Sunday, Nov. 1, the team said he was being evaluated for a neck injury. They have provided few specific medical updates since, citing respect for Campbell's family. After being off Tuesday, Lions players return to practice Wednesday, Nov. 4. Head coach Dan Campbell is scheduled to have a press conference at 1 p.m.

Here is what the Lions and Dan Campbell have said about Jack Campbell's injury:

➤ In a postgame radio interview with Lions Radio Network's Brad Galli, Dan Campbell said Jack Campbell was alert and breathing on his way off the field.

➤ In his postgame press conference, Campbell said: "Thoughts and prayers are with Jack and his family. He's being taken care of. We don't have any new information. We'll keep you updated as this goes, but we're thinking about him."

➤ At 7:08 p.m. on Sunday night, the team released this statement: "Jack Campbell is resting and will remain in a local hospital tonight, for continued evaluation and monitoring. The team will provide further updates as we have them."

➤ At 2:31 p.m. on Monday, the Lions announced: "Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital. Preliminary indications are positive and out of respect for Jack and his family we will not share further information at this time."

➤ At his press conference about half an hour later, Dan Campbell referred to the team's statement and said, "It's positive. So your prayers are working. Please continue to do that and we'll leave it at that. So, just continue to pray for him, but it is positive news on Jack."

➤ Asked if he could say any more on Jack Campbell’s injury, the coach said, “I can't, so I'm not going to.” He added, "The team knows what's going on. I've given it to the captains.”

➤ At his Monday press conference, Dan Campbell also said he visited Jack Campbell and his family at the hospital on Sunday night: "It was good. It was positive. Got to see his parents, talk to his wife. And everybody's in good spirits. And it's about the recovery and it's a small setback, that's the family. They're very positive.”

BEREA ― Deshaun Watson may not be available for the Browns when they face the New Orleans Saints. The Browns announced the quarterback has been placed in concussion protocol.

"During the first quarter of Sunday's game against the Steelers, Deshaun took a helmet-to-helmet hit," the team said in a statement. "The ATC spotter called down to the sideline, and the Unaffiliated Neurotrauma Consultant (UNC) administered a gameday concussion evaluation. Deshaun was cleared by the UNC and returned on the Browns' next offensive series.

"As part of the protocol, the team's medical staff evaluated him again postgame and Monday morning. Both times he showed no symptoms, passed his evaluations, and was cleared. On Tuesday morning, he reported to the medical staff that he began experiencing concussion symptoms Monday night and was immediately placed in the concussion protocol."

Subscribe to Browns Insider newsletter

If Watson can't go, the expectation is backup Shedeur Sanders would start with Cleveland plays at the New Orleans Saints Nov. 8. Sanders came on for two plays in the Browns' Week 8 loss at the Pittsburgh Steelers when Watson left the game to be evaluated for a concussion.

The hit in question came on the third play of the game. Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker came in high and hit Watson helmet to helmet with 13:33 remaining in the first quarter, drawing a roughing the passer penalty.

Watson was down on a knee for a moment, then got up and initially waved off Sanders. However, the independent evaluator had him pulled from the game to be checked for a concussion, although he was out of the evaluation and had his helmet by the time the possession ended.

"No, I mean they were just checking," Watson said immediately after the game. "They were doing NFL protocol, checking for concussion. The brain is one of the most important things in the body outside the heart and the lungs. But they had to do their job and had to do the evaluation, and we did that and then I was able to go back in."

Sanders played a total of four plays on the Browns' first drive, which ended on a fumble by tight end Harold Fannin Jr. upon replay challenge. He was 2-for-2 for 2 yards on the drive.

Deshaun Watson returned to game after helmet-to-helmet hit

Watson came back in the game on the next possession, whcih started with 11:14 remaining in the first quarter. He played the remainder of the game, finishing 27-of-39 for 324 yards, the most passing yards of Watson's Browns career and second consecutive 300-yard passing game.

The Steelers sacked Watson eight times, matching a career high for the quarterback. He's been sacked a league-high 33 times, and, according to Pro Football Focus, been hit another seven times on pass attempts while being pressured 130 times on 307 dropbacks.

Deshaun Watson's statistics through seven games in 2026

Watson had quarterbacked the Browns to five fourth-quarter comebacks, including four in which they scored the go-ahead points in the final two minutes of the game. He leads the NFL in passer rating (130.3), passing yards (448), completion percentage (75.5) and completions (37) in the final two minutes of either half.

For the season, Watson has completed 163-of-249 passes for 1,806 yards, an average of 258 yards per game. He's thrown seven touchdowns to three interceptions, while posting a 91.2 rating.

Watson has added 217 rushing yards on 51 carries and one score. His ability to run and extend plays was a key to the Browns' fourth-quarter successes in winning five of six between Weeks 2 and 6, although it also led to extra hits.

Deshaun Watson also missed 1 play vs. Carolina Panthers

The four plays in Pittsburgh marked the second time Watson missed time in game due to a roughing the passer penalty on an opponent. He also missed one play in the Week 3 game at the Carolina Panthers after being hit by linebacker Bobby Okereke with 2:39 remaining in the game, a penalty which negated what could've been a game-sealing interception for the Panthers, who led 18-13 at the time.

Sanders replaced Watson for that one play, completing a pass to running back Quinshon Judkins for no gain. He returned to the game on the next play, which came after the two-minute warning, and threw a go-ahead touchdown to Fannin with 1:44 remaining.

Another Deshaun Watson injury in Cleveland

Watson's play, and more specifically the Browns' winning, to start the season has thawed some of the icy feelings that had developed over four essentially lost seasons since they acquired the quarterback from the Houston Texans in 2022. Over those four seasons, he had started just 19 of a possible 68 games because of suspension and two season-ending injuries — a 2023 shoulder injury that required surgery and two Achilles tears in 2024, the latter which cost him all of 2025.

A head injury makes the question of how many games Watson could miss an unknown. It could be anywhere from no games missed to a significant time.

There was also the more than two dozen lawsuits ― all since settled ― by women in the Houston area alleging sexual assault and/or sexual misconduct during massage appointments, all of which led to an 11-game suspension from the league to open his Cleveland career.

Shedeur Sanders missed out on starting job in preseason

Sanders spent the entire offseason and training camp locked in a competition with Watson for the starting job. At multiple times during the competition, it appeared as though the second-year pro might even win the job.

However, after each quarterback started a preseason game, Browns coach Todd Monken named Watson the starter. Sanders was installed as the No. 2, while rookie Taylen Green was initially the No. 3 while Dillon Gabriel was on injured reserve with a back injury.

There was speculation flying around the Browns following the opening loss at the Jacksonville Jaguars that they would go to Sanders as the starter for the home opener against the Panthers if Watson's didn't play well in Week 2 at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. That ended up being the first of Watson's five fourth-quarter comebacks, as he threw for 238 yards and two touchdowns in a 23-19 win.

Sanders has spent most of his time since the Browns transitioned out of training camp and into the regular season getting some work with the scout team in practice. Otherwise, most of the reps have gone to Watson.

Shedeur Sanders took similar path to start as rookie in 2025

It was a similar situation as to what Sanders went through as a rookie in 2025 after he was promoted to the backup role behind Gabriel in Week 6 of that season. It was a concussion that Gabriel suffered late in the first half of the Browns' Week 11 home loss to the Baltimore Ravens that led to Sanders getting the starting job for the remainder of the season.

Sanders started the final seven games of his rookie season. The Browns went 3-4 in those games, including wins in his first career start Week 12 at the Las Vegas Raiders and a season-ending win streak against the Steelers at home and at the Cincinnati Bengals.

The fifth-round pick out of the University of Colorado completed 56.6% of his passes for 1,400 yards with seven touchdowns, 10 interceptions, a 68.1 passer rating and 23 sacks as a rookie. He was added to the AFC Pro Bowl roster the week of the game.

Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol. Shedeur Sanders could start as Browns QB

The Cleveland Browns placed Deshaun Watson in the NFL's concussion protocol, putting the team's starting quarterback in jeopardy of missing the team's Week 9 game against the New Orleans Saints.

The Browns announced Watson's placement in concussion protocol in a statement released on Wednesday, Nov. 4.

"During the first quarter of Sunday's game against the Steelers, Deshaun took a helmet-to-helmet hit," the Browns statement read. "The ATC spotter called down to the sideline, and the Unaffiliated Neurotrauma Consultant (UNC) administered a gameday concussion evaluation. Deshaun was cleared by the UNC and returned on the Browns' next offensive series."

"As part of the protocol, the team's medical staff evaluated him again postgame and Monday morning," the statement continued. "Both times he showed no symptoms, passed his evaluations, and was cleared. On Tuesday morning, he reported to the medical staff that he began experiencing concussion symptoms Monday night and was immediately placed in the concussion protocol."

Watson has guided the Browns to a surprising 5-3 record in 2026 while completing 65.5% of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven touchdowns and three interceptions. If he can't play, backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders will likely be handed the reins against the Saints.

Here's more to know about Watson's injury, the NFL's concussion protocol and how the Browns' quarterback depth chart shakes out behind him.

What is the NFL's concussion protocol?

The NFL's concussion protocol outlines a five-step process for players who have been diagnosed with a concussion to return to action. The steps are as follows:

Phase 1: Symptom-limited activity (introduction of light aerobic activity)

Phase 2: Aerobic exercise (more than 20 minutes of moderate to strenuous resistance)

Phase 3: Football-specific exercise

Phase 4: Club-based non-contact training drills (participating in all non-contact practice drills)

Phase 5: Full football activity (clearance)

Once a player completes the process and is cleared for full participation by his team's physician, he must also be seen and separately cleared by an NFL- and NFLPA-approved Independent Neurological Consultant (INC). A player cannot return to action until he is cleared by an independent physician.

There is no official timetable for a player to progress through the NFL's concussion protocol, though NBC Sports and CBS Sports report the median recovery for NFL players is about nine days. Such a timeline would put Watson in danger of missing the Browns' Week 9 game, so his practice status will need to be monitored closely.

Will Shedeur Sanders start for Browns in Week 9?

If Watson can't clear the NFL's concussion protocol ahead of the Browns' Week 9 game against the Saints, backup quarterback Sanders would be expected to start.

Sanders, a fifth-round pick from the 2025 NFL Draft, has played sparingly in 2026 after losing the starting job to Watson during the preseason. As a rookie, Sanders completed 56.6% of his passes for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions while leading the Browns to a 3-4 record across seven starts.

Browns QB depth chart

The Browns are one of just a few NFL teams to have four quarterbacks on their 53-man roster. Below is a look at the pecking order within the unit.

Deshaun Watson

Shedeur Sanders

Dillon Gabriel

Taylen Green

Like Sanders, Gabriel was selected in the 2025 NFL Draft. The third-rounder made six starts as a rookie, posting a 1-5 record while completing 59.5% of his passes for 937 yards, seven touchdowns and two interceptions. The lefty missed the start of the 2026 NFL season with a back injury but returned from IR ahead of Cleveland's Week 8 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Meanwhile, Green – a sixth-round rookie out of Arkansas – has served as the Browns' thrid-string quarterback for most of the season without Gabriel available. The 24-year-old has yet to play an NFL snap.

BEREA ― Quarterback Deshaun Watson is the latest Cleveland Browns player who has been placed into the NFL's concussion protocol this season. Once they're in the protocol, there are specific steps that must be followed before the player can return to the field for a game.

The NFL and the NFL Players Association jointly designed specific guidelines to be followed by every team with regards to players with head injuries. It dates back to the 2011 collective bargaining agreement.

The primary part of the protocol is the return-to-participation piece. It's a five-step process that must be checked off, with an extra step after he's cleared by the team physician that requires that the player, according to the guidelines, "must be seen and separately cleared by an Independent Neurological Consultant (INC), jointly approved by the NFL and NFLPA, who is not affiliated with any NFL club. Until cleared by this independent physician, a player may not return to contact practice or play in an NFL game."

Subscribe to Browns Insider newsletter

The timeline in terms of how long it takes to pass through the protocol can vary wildly. The Browns have had multiple players who entered the protocol on a Sunday or Monday and managed to play the following week, a list that includes wide receiver KC Concepcion after his Week 5 helmet-to-helmet hit by New York Jets' safety Minkah Fitzpatrick and, just this past week, right tackle Tytus Howard after his Week 6 concussion at the Tennessee Titans.

So, what's the specific return-to-participation protocol that the Browns and Watson must follow? Here's the specific steps as spelled out by the league and NFLPA:

Phase 1: Symptom Limited Activity

The player is prescribed rest, limiting or, if necessary, avoiding activities (both physical and cognitive) which increase or aggravate symptoms. Under athletic training staff supervision, limited stretching and balance training can be introduced, progressing to light aerobic exercise, all as tolerated.

Phase 2: Aerobic exercise

Under direct oversight of the team’s medical staff, the player should begin graduated cardiovascular exercise and may also engage in dynamic stretching and balance training. Neurocognitive and balance testing can be administered after completion of Phase Two and the results should be interpreted as back to baseline.

Phase 3: Football-specific exercise

The player continues with supervised cardiovascular exercises that are increased and may mimic sport-specific activities, and supervised strength training is introduced. The player is allowed to practice with the team in sport-specific exercise for 30 minutes or less with ongoing and careful monitoring.

Phase 4: Club-based non-contact training drills

The player continues cardiovascular, strength and balance training, team-based sports-specific exercise, and participates in non-contact football activities (e.g. throwing, catching, running, and other position-specific activities). Neurocognitive and balance testing should be completed no later than the end of Phase Four with the results interpreted as back to baseline.

Phase 5: Full football activity/clearance

Upon clearance by the Club physician for full football activity involving contact, the player must be examined by the Independent Neurological Consultant (INC) assigned to his Club. If the INC concurs with the Club physician that the player’s concussion has resolved, he may participate in his Club’s next practice or game.

text:
The Washington Commanders lost a second defensive line starter for the season in less than a week as Javon Kinlaw underwent season-ending knee surgery, a source told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Kinlaw, who played end in their base defense and tackle in their nickel package, injured his MCL in a Week 6 loss at San Francisco.

Two days before the Week 8 win over Philadelphia, Daron Payne fractured his foot in what was described as a "fluke injury" during a light Friday practice. He, too, is out for the season. Like Kinlaw, Payne started at end in their 3-4 base front and played tackle in their nickel package.

It's another blow for the Commanders (2-4-1), who host the Rams (4-4) on Sunday.

Kinlaw, signed to a three-year deal in the 2025 offseason, had started 23 consecutive games for Washington before injuring his knee. He was considered strong against the run and had recorded two tackles for loss. He recorded a career-best 5.2% of his tackles at or behind the line of scrimmage -- only six defensive linemen had a higher percentage.

He had helped more as a pass rusher this season with one sack and three quarterback hits. He did not record a sack last season and was on pace for the most quarterback hits in his career; his previous high was six in 2023 with the 49ers.

The Commanders added depth along the defensive line this season with Charles Omenihu and nose tackle Tim Settle. Omenihu and Deatrich Wise Jr. replaced Payne and Kinlaw in the starting lineup in Washington's 27-10 win over Philadelphia last Sunday.

The Commanders continue to lose key starters. Washington also lost its top receiver, Terry McLaurin, to a torn patellar tendon in his left knee in Week 6. Left tackle Laremy Tunsil suffered a torn triceps on Aug. 8. The Commanders have not yet ruled him out for the season; last week, coach Dan Quinn said Tunsil has a checkup in a couple of weeks that will determine whether there's a chance he could return late in the season.

title: Browns place QB Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol - Sportsnet.ca
description:
If Watson is not cleared in time for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints, Shedeur Sanders would get his first start of the season.
Watson took a helmet-to-helmet hit during the first quarter of last week's 27-6 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers.
The Browns said Wednesday morning that Watson received evaluations after Sunday's game and Monday morning.
Watson told the medical staff Tuesday morning he began experiencing symptoms Monday night when he was placed in the concussion protocol.
He started the final seven games of his rookie season last year, going 3-4 with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions.

Browns place QB Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol

Associated PressNovember 04, 2026 - 11:18am

BEREA, Ohio — Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson has been placed in the concussion protocol after experiencing symptoms Monday night.

If Watson is not cleared in time for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints, Shedeur Sanders would get his first start of the season.

Watson took a helmet-to-helmet hit during the first quarter of last week's 27-6 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. The independent certified athletic trainer watching the game from the press box called down to the Browns sideline and Watson was given a gameday concussion evaluation and cleared by the unaffiliated neurotrauma consultant.

The 10-year veteran returned to the game and completed 27 of 39 passes for 324 yards, his second straight 300-yard game.

The Browns said Wednesday morning that Watson received evaluations after Sunday's game and Monday morning. He was cleared after showing no symptoms. Watson told the medical staff Tuesday morning he began experiencing symptoms Monday night when he was placed in the concussion protocol.

Sanders was in for four plays against the Steelers, and completed both of his passes for 2 yards. He started the final seven games of his rookie season last year, going 3-4 with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions.

text:
Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders may be getting more than a handful of snaps in Week 9, when his team visits the Saints.

The Browns have announced that starting quarterback Deshaun Watson is in the concussion protocol.

“During the first quarter of Sunday’s game against the Steelers, Deshaun took a helmet-to-helmet hit,” the team said in a statement released on Wednesday morning. “The ATC spotter called down to the sideline, and the Unaffiliated Neurotrauma Consultant (UNC) administered a gameday concussion evaluation. Deshaun was cleared by the UNC and returned on the Browns’ next offensive series. As part of the protocol, the team’s medical staff evaluated him again postgame and Monday morning. Both times he showed no symptoms, passed his evaluations, and was cleared. On Tuesday morning, he reported to the medical staff that he began experiencing concussion symptoms Monday night and was immediately placed in the concussion protocol.”

Watson will remain in the concussion protocol until he clears the various steps. Until then, Sanders will presumably be the starter — unless the coaching staff decides to pivot to Dillon Gabriel.

The development comes not long after Sanders hired an agent for the first time, presumably in an effort to secure a trade to a new team. For now, he’ll get a chance to make the case to become the eventual starter for the Browns. Or to attract interest elsewhere in him once 2027 rolls around.

For the 5-3 Browns, it’s a significant development. They need to keep pace with the 6-2 Steelers and 5-2 Bengals. Picking up a fourth loss without Watson (who eventually threw for 324 yards in the 27-6 loss at Pittsburgh) will make that harder to accomplish.

text:
The 2026 NFL season has reached its halfway point, but injuries continue to trouble several teams. Week 8 brought some major setbacks, with several players leaving games early and others facing long spells on the sidelines. Now, as teams get ready for Week 9, the injury list has become an important talking point.

Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is one of the biggest concerns after hurting his thumb against the Buffalo Bills. His backup, Tyler Huntley, also suffered an injury. This leaves Baltimore with a serious problem at quarterback ahead of its Thursday night game against Jacksonville. Meanwhile, Arizona Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love is expected to miss several weeks, while New York Jets running back Breece Hall could finally make his return.

The official NFL injury reports will become clearer as teams share their practice updates. Baltimore and Jacksonville have less time to prepare because they play on Thursday Night Football.

Fantasy managers and NFL fans should watch the final reports before kickoff. A player who practices early in the week is not always ready to play on game day.

Here is a closer look at the latest NFL Week 9 injury updates.

Lamar Jackson’s injury creates a quarterback crisis in Baltimore

The biggest injury concern heading into Week 9 comes from the Baltimore Ravens’ quarterback room.

Lamar Jackson returned in Week 8 after missing three games with an ankle injury. However, his comeback against Buffalo ended almost as soon as it began. Jackson suffered a thumb injury on his first offensive play. He now needs surgery and could move to injured reserve, which may end his regular season. Either way, he’ll be out for a long time.

Head coach Jesse Minter confirmed that Jackson’s injury could keep him out for the rest of the campaign. He will miss at least four games while he recovers.

But Jackson was not Baltimore’s only injury concern. Backup quarterback Tyler Huntley also left the game with a turf toe injury. He is expected to miss an extended period and will not be ready for the Week 9 matchup.

Rookie Joe Fagnano came into the game, but he struggled to get the offense going. He completed just 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and threw an interception. He also picked up an ankle injury. However, head coach Minter has said that Fagnano is expected to start against Jacksonville.

Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray is another player to watch after dealing with a hamstring issue in Week 8. Los Angeles Rams’ Matthew Stafford also has an arm injury, but the team will need to provide more updates about his availability.

Running Backs: Breece Hall nears return as Jeremiyah Love heads to IR

Running back injuries are another big talking point ahead of NFL Week 9.

Breece Hall (Jets): Hall missed Week 8 even though many expected him to return against the Raiders. He is dealing with a quadriceps injury, but he could finally return against Kansas City. Braelon Allen has done a good job in Hall’s absence. He ranks as the RB5 in half-PPR scoring from Weeks 5-8. Even if Hall returns, Allen could still have a role in the offense.

Jeremiyah Love (Cardinals): Arizona suffered another setback as Love picked up a high-ankle sprain during the overtime win over Dallas. The rookie could miss four to five weeks and is expected to land on injured reserve. Bam Knight also suffered a concussion and is doubtful for Week 9. With both backs injured, Tyler Allgeier could lead the backfield. James Conner could also return later.

Bhayshul Tuten (Jaguars): Tuten missed back-to-back practices on Monday and Tuesday because of ankle and foot injuries. This is a concern as the team will face Baltimore on Thursday and has very little time to prepare. Tuten had a big performance in Week 8, recording 159 total yards and two touchdowns on 18 touches. If he cannot play, Chris Rodriguez Jr. could get more chances.

Christian McCaffrey (49ers): McCaffrey enters Week 9 with a mild hamstring strain after San Francisco’s bye week. He is expected to play against the Raiders, but the team could limit his workload. Rookie Kaelon Black may get more chances as the 49ers look to keep their star running back fresh.

Other running backs to watch include Cam Skattebo (Giants), Kyle Monangai (Bears), David Montgomery (Texans), Travis Etienne Jr. (Saints), TreVeyon Henderson (Patriots) and Brian Robinson Jr. (Falcons).

Wide Receivers and Tight Ends: Several key players under watch

The injury concerns do not stop with the running backs. Several wide receivers and tight ends are also dealing with fitness problems ahead of the weekend.

Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson broke a rib during the Week 8 Thursday night game against Carolina. The team took him to the hospital, but he made a surprising return and finished the game. Watson caught eight passes for 113 yards on 10 targets.

If he plays, another hit could make his injury worse. Matthew Golden, Tucker Kraft and Savion Williams are the options available in case Watson misses out.

Arizona’s Michael Wilson is also dealing with broken ribs after the win over Dallas. He seems ready to play through the injury, but his availability against Seattle remains uncertain.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receiver Emeka Egbuka could also return after missing the previous two games with foot and concussion concerns. His return would give Tampa Bay another option in the passing game against Chicago.

Other wide receivers on the injury watch list include DeVonta Smith (Eagles), Jakobi Meyers (Jaguars), AJ Brown (Patriots), Deebo Samuel (49ers) and Mike Evans (49ers).

At tight end, Dallas Cowboys’ Jake Ferguson suffered a low-ankle sprain against Arizona in Week 8 and did not return to the game. If he misses Week 9, Brevyn Span-Ford could get more playing time.

New England’s Hunter Henry and Los Angeles Rams’ Colby Parkinson are also dealing with injuries. Their teams will need to share more updates before the weekend.

Season-ending injuries and players on IR

Several teams have already lost important players for the rest of the season. These absences have forced teams to change their plans and depend more on backup players.

Here are some of the major names who are out or on injured reserve:

Jaxson Dart (Giants, QB): Knee injury; expected to miss the rest of the regular season.

Jalen Hurts (Eagles, QB): Blood clots; out for the season.

Ricky Pearsall (49ers, WR): Knee injury; out for the season.

Terry McLaurin (Commanders, WR): Knee injury; out for the season.

Jaylin Noel (Texans, WR): Turf toe; expected to miss the rest of the regular season.

Jayden Higgins (Texans, WR): Torn ACL; out for the season.

Davante Adams (Rams, WR): Ruptured hamstring tendon; placed on injured reserve.

Romeo Doubs (Patriots, WR): Shoulder injury; on injured reserve.

Jalen McMillan (Buccaneers, WR): Knee injury; on injured reserve.

James Conner (Cardinals, RB): Foot injury; on injured reserve.

Travis Etienne Jr. (Saints, RB): Hamstring injury; on injured reserve.

Backup players now have a chance to step up, while coaches must find new ways to keep their offenses running.

What to watch before Week 9 kickoff

The next few practice reports will play a big role for NFL teams and fantasy football managers. Lamar Jackson’s absence is already a major blow for Baltimore. The possible returns of Breece Hall, Christian McCaffrey, Bhayshul Tuten and Mike Evans could have a big impact on their teams in Week 9.

Arizona must also find a solution at running back after losing Jeremiyah Love and possibly Bam Knight. Green Bay will also wait for updates on Christian Watson as he recovers from broken ribs.

Players who miss early-week practices can still return for game day. However, those with serious injuries may need more time to recover.

As Week 9 approaches, the final injury reports will help teams understand which players are ready to return and who will remain on the sidelines.

text:
The National Football League (NFL)’s expanding interest in staging games overseas is part of a plan to strengthen the game’s appeal and market globally, but it also has implications for player performance and injury risk.

When the New England Patriots square off against the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany, on Nov. 15, it will be one of a record nine regular season games played overseas this season. The 2026 schedule includes games played in three first-time countries — Australia, Brazil, and France — as well as Germany, United Kingdom, Spain, and Mexico.

“Bringing games into more markets gives consumers direct exposure to the NFL, whether it is a completely new experience or simply a rare opportunity to see a game in person,” says Eun Kang, Ph.D., associate professor of Marketing. “A sold-out stadium tells us people are interested in the event, but it does not necessarily mean they have become NFL fans.”

RELATED ARTICLE: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel’s path to success demonstrates that leadership is a learned skill

The real measure of success is whether consumers continue watching games, follow a team or individual players, engage with NFL content, and eventually develop a longer-term relationship with the sport, says Kang. That’s a bigger hurdle for American football, which has no real cultural roots outside of the United States and Canada and has rules and traditions that are hard for newcomers to grasp.

“Sports fandom is highly emotional and is often tied to geography, family, tradition, and identity,” Kang says. “In many countries, people grow up supporting the same soccer club as their parents, friends, or local community. That connection creates a sense of belonging and makes the relationship with the team more personal. An NFL team from thousands of miles away does not automatically have that same emotional bond.”

Christian Fauria, a professional in residence who teaches within Bryant’s Communication, Media, and Sports Industries department, compares overseas NFL games to the “friendly” exhibition games that international soccer teams have staged in the U.S. to boost interest in teams playing in the upper echelon of the sport, such as the English Premier League.

“The merchandising, the games, the TV rights are where I think the NFL is headed, because that's where the big money is,” says Fauria, who played tight end for four NFL teams over a 13-year career and won two Super Bowl championships with the New England Patriots. “In-person game experiences are great, but if you look at every network and entertainment platform, the one thing that isn't going [away] is live sports.”

RELATED ARTICLE: Patriots QB Drake Maye urges college students to live in the moment, lean into gratitude, at sold-out campus talk

Fauria doesn’t expect the NFL to place a franchise overseas soon, but he does see huge potential for growing the sport through promotion of flag football, which will make its debut in the 2028 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles.

“The NFL is putting a lot of time and money into flag football,” he says, noting that while college or pro football isn’t intrinsic to the sports culture in other markets, flag football can generate broad appeal across genders. “The NFL doesn't care if people move on to playing tackle football. They would be perfectly happy to have people play flag football and then watch NFL games.”

“The NFL doesn't care if people move on to playing tackle football. They would be perfectly happy to have people play flag football and then watch NFL games.”

Kang agrees.

“The NFL can become a global entertainment brand by getting consumers in countries such as Germany, Brazil, and Australia to watch games and support NFL teams. But football only becomes a truly international sport when people in those countries begin playing it,” she says. “That is why the growth of flag football and youth participation may be just as important in the long run as international NFL games.”

Challenges are physical as well as cultural

The NFL has been playing games in foreign markets for more than two decades: the first regular season game played outside the U.S. was in Mexico City in 2005, and the first European game was held in London in 2007.

Over the years, teams have become better acclimated to the travel involved in these one-off games.

“The players have been conditioned that it’s part of the schedule, and they account for it like Monday Night Football or Thursday Night Football,” says Fauria.

However, the schedule can still be punishing. The Los Angeles Rams, for example, were widely criticized for their decision to fly to Melbourne, Australia, just 24 hours before their Sept. 10 game against the San Francisco 49ers, who arrived a full week before. The 49ers handily beat a noticeably fatigued Rams team, 27-7, in that game.

RELATED ARTICLE: For Bulldogs kicker Nick Stoyanovich ’29, success is a family affair

“Long flights and time zone shifts disrupt the circadian rhythm, the body’s internal clock that regulates sleep, body temperature, hormone release, and alertness,” says Benjamin Fry, lecturer of Biological and Biomedical Sciences. “Physically, athletes can experience shortened or fragmented sleep, fatigue, slower reaction time, reduced power output, stiffness from prolonged sitting, dehydration, and digestive problems.”

Mentally, jet lag can affect attention, memory, decision-making, and mood, Fry adds: “Those are the skills football depends on, from reading a defense to recalling a complex playbook in a split second.”

Fry says research findings about the impact of travel on sports performance are inconclusive but says a common rule of thumb is to allow one day of adjustment per time zone crossed.

“Melbourne’s 17-hour difference is more extreme, and even a week does not allow for full adaptation,” he notes.

“As the NFL increases international games, the interesting frontier is direct physiological monitoring linked to performance and injury,” says Fry, pointing out that few studies exist that track NFL players' sleep, circadian phase, or neuromuscular recovery.

“As the NFL increases international games, the interesting frontier is direct physiological monitoring linked to performance and injury."

Likewise, he says, current research on injury patterns in the NFL often examine season-long travel and may miss the short, post-travel window where fatigue peaks.

“We still don't know if jet lag affects a lineman's explosive power differently than a quarterback's decision-making, or how to optimize a protocol when half your roster adapts in two days and half needs five,” he says. “The research exists in other sports and in labs, but translating it to football's week-to-week reality remains more art than science.”

text:
The Baltimore Ravens are now down their top two quarterbacks for the foreseeable future.

According to ESPN, the turf toe injury that backup quarterback Tyler Huntley suffered against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday is season-ending. Ravens coach Jesse Minter had announced Tuesday that No. 3 QB Joe Fagnano would start Thursday night against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Lamar Jackson was placed on injured reserve Tuesday after suffering an injury to his thumb on his throwing hand on the first offensive play of the game in the loss to the Bills. Jackson needs surgery on his right thumb.

Huntley immediately replaced Jackson, but he suffered his turf toe injury before halftime and didn't return to the game. Before his injury, Huntley attempted just four passes.

Huntley made three starts in 2026 as Jackson was sidelined with an ankle injury. The Bills game was Jackson's first start since he suffered that ankle injury on Oct. 4 against the Tennessee Titans.

Fagnano is an undrafted rookie from UConn who took his first NFL regular-season snaps after taking over for Huntley. He was 10 of 21 for 91 yards and an interception. He practiced Tuesday with a brace on his right ankle after injuring that during the game.

Behind Fagnano, the Ravens signed former practice squad quarterback Austin Reed and also added Kedon Slovis to the roster with Jackson and Huntley out.

Huntley, 28, has been Jackson's primary backup for his entire career outside of spending the 2024 season with the Miami Dolphins. Over six years with the Ravens, he's appeared in 30 games and made 14 starts, infamously making the 2022 Pro Bowl after appearing in six games that season.

Baltimore is now 4-4 after three straight losses and the absence of Jackson and Huntley could end up making their hopes of winning the AFC North disappear as every other team in the division is above .500. After playing Jacksonville this week, the Ravens host the Chargers on Monday Night Football.

title: DaVon Hamilton injury puts A'Mauri Washington in Jaguars' NFL Draft spotlight
description:
Ladies and gentlemen, defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton is out for the foreseeable future.
His work over the nose of the football was one big reason the Jacksonville Jaguars had the top-ranked run defense in the NFL.
On the business side, this news is terrible because the 29-year-old is in the final year of his contract.
Without the NFL's best answer to the run game's return to prominence, the Jaguars could be in for a long back half of the season.
A'Mauri Washington could help the Jaguars erase the league's feature backs Right now, multiple outlets have Washington ranked as one of the 40 best draft prospects in America.
text:
Ladies and gentlemen, defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton is out for the foreseeable future. That's a big blow for multiple reasons. For one, he was playing the best football of his pro career. His work over the nose of the football was one big reason the Jacksonville Jaguars had the top-ranked run defense in the NFL. On the business side, this news is terrible because the 29-year-old is in the final year of his contract.

Without the NFL's best answer to the run game's return to prominence, the Jaguars could be in for a long back half of the season. Obviously, we'd all like James Gladstone to find an answer to this problem now. Unfortunately, Jacksonville's current finances might not allow him to do so. That means Liam Coen and Anthony Campanile will have to hold on to dear life while the front office looks towards the future.

Luckily, the future could be bright because of an athletic stud from the Big 10.

A'Mauri Washington could help the Jaguars erase the league's feature backs

Right now, multiple outlets have Washington ranked as one of the 40 best draft prospects in America. Sports Illustrated's Gilberto Manzano ranked the Oregon defensive tackle 33rd on his list of the Top 100 players hoping to be selected next spring.

In his blurb on Washington, Manzano writes that "The 6'3", 319-pounder knows how to give opposing offensive linemen problems with elite power and burst. He has plenty of experience, appearing in 45 games since arriving at Oregon in 2023.

However, the journalist also says that "[Washington] needs to finish more consistently, considering he has only 1.5 sacks in his collegiate career, including none this season."

Now, before you roast me, we have to remember two things. First, the Jaguars are going to win the AFC South. That means they're going to be hosting a playoff game and, at worst, make their picks in the middle of the draft order. Second, DaVon Hamilton is a run-stopping behemoth who was underappreciated until Jacksonville's recent rise.

Washington could step in and be a Week 1 starter with his experience and skill set. If the Jags decide to fill a major need instead of grabbing the best player available, the Detroit native could give Jacksonville up to five years of relief as they work to address other issues.

And, man, the Jaguars have a lot of issues

The Jags will have to use the draft to improve the roster for the next year or so as it gets its finances right. If Gladstone and his staff decide to move some money around to make a splash trade, they'll probably be looking for a true pass rusher or a dominant man corner. However, those aren't the only position groups that need more depth or a flat-out upgrade.

Eric Murray's recent injury gave Rayuan Lane III an opportunity to have his best performance yet. Time will tell if he can start full-time, but Jacksonville also needs to make a decision on Antonio Johnson and his long-term future. Along with that, Ventrell Miller and Anton Harrison's expiring deals could turn a bad situation into a crisis if they aren't retained.

This is probably when I should be optimistic and say, "At least Gladstone will have a big batch of picks to work with in 2027!" As of now, Jax has nine draft selections, including three compensatory picks. However, six of them are in Rounds 4-7. That means Jimmy Stones will have to find numerous diamonds in the rough and work against his preferred strategy of elevating the floor.

The Jags being a top-heavy outfit isn't a bad thing. That being said, relying so much on your best 15 or so players comes with massive risks. We're seeing the cost of those risks with DaVon Hamilton's situation and, hopefully, we don't have to feel them with Bhayshul Tuten as well.

The front office will be able to solve one problem with the upcoming draft, but it doesn't look like they'll be able to solve them all.

Fagnano will be the second undrafted quarterback to make his first career NFL start in primetime.

text:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Tyler "Snoop" Huntley is out for the season with a turf toe injury on his right foot, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport on Wednesday, further devastating the Baltimore Ravens' quarterback room.

Tests revealed that Huntley needs surgery, sources said.

Huntley, the Ravens' top backup, was injured in the second quarter of Sunday's 36-10 loss at Buffalo when Bills defensive tackle Ed Oliver twisted the quarterback to the ground after he got rid of the ball.

In addition to Huntley's injury, starting quarterback Lamar Jackson is out indefinitely with a right thumb injury that he sustained on his first snap Sunday. It is "potentially" a season-ending injury, coach Jesse Minter said.

With Jackson and Huntley both out, undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano will make his first career start Thursday night at the Jacksonville Jaguars. Fagnano wore a brace on his right ankle during Tuesday's practice but is set to play after being a full participant.

Fagnano will be the second undrafted quarterback to make his first career NFL start in primetime. The first to do so was Cooper Rush, who led the Dallas Cowboys in 2021 to a game-winning drive against the Minnesota Vikings.

The injuries to Jackson and Huntley have left Baltimore with extremely inexperienced options at quarterback. The Ravens' top three quarterbacks -- Fagnano, Austin Reed and Kedon Slovis -- have combined for 23 career pass attempts, 44 total snaps and zero touchdown passes in the NFL.

Reed was signed to Baltimore's practice squad Monday, and Slovis was signed off the Green Bay Packers' practice squad Tuesday.

Huntley, 28, had started three games for the Ravens this season while filling in for Jackson. He led Baltimore to an overtime comeback win in Atlanta on Oct. 11.

text:
Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell remained hospitalized Monday as team officials hinted that the standout defender was recovering from a scary injury he sustained Sunday.

The team said “preliminary indications are positive” about 24 hours after a seemingly routine tackle left Campbell face down and motionless on the Ford Field turf.

“Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital,” the Lions said in a statement Monday afternoon. “Preliminary indications are positive and out of respect for Jack and his family we will not share further information at this time.”

Coach Dan Campbell, who is not related, thanked fans for their ongoing concern.

“It’s positive,” he said Monday of Campbell’s prognosis. “So your prayers are working. Please continue to do that.”

Coach Campbell declined to discuss details of his player’s injury. He and other players visited him at the hospital Sunday night, the coach said.

“It was positive. ... Got to see his parents, talk to his wife,” he said. “Everybody’s in good spirits, and it’s about the recovery.”

On the first play of the fourth quarter, Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray connected with tight end T.J. Hockenson for a 10-yard gain, with Campbell and teammate Eric O’Neill bringing Hockenson down in what appeared to be a routine tackle.

But Campbell, 26, of Cedar Falls, Iowa, immediately became prone, face down on the field, and he was not moving as medical staffers rushed to his aid. He was strapped into a medical cart and driven away.

Campbell showed proper form, with his head up, in making the by-the-book tackle. But it appeared his head and neck might have been forced backward as his helmet made contact with Hockenson’s left hip.

Campbell most likely made contact with Hockenson’s hipbone, a rigid angle of the body with little give, said Dr. Robert Glatter, an emergency physician at Northwell Health’s Lenox Hill Hospital in New York City.

That head-on-hip collision probably caused a spinal cord concussion at about the C7 vertebra, Glatter told NBC News. It appeared that Campbell was breathing on his own Sunday, which in itself was a hopeful sign.

“If someone’s not breathing, then you worry about a high cervical injury, C1, C2, and those can be deadly right off the bat,” said Glatter, a former sideline physician for the New York Jets.

“If I had to guess, it’s a C6 or a C7 type of injury just based on the fact he was breathing and his vitals seem to be stable.”

The serious injury cast a pall over the Detroit locker room Sunday as players cut short their celebration of a dramatic 19-15 victory over the division rival Vikings.

Coach Campbell had been jubilantly shouting out his players before he shifted the postgame address to their injured teammate.

“I do not have any more information on Jack,” he told players. “We don’t know anything else at this point. So here’s what I want to do: We’re going to take a knee. I want to pray for Jack. Let’s keep him in our thoughts and prayers.”
